claim: A large force always creates large rotation, even when it is applied right next to the pivot.
reality: Torque depends on both force magnitude and moment arm. A large force with almost no lever arm can produce very little rotation.
whyItHappens: Students often import straight-line force intuition into rotational problems and ignore geometry.
coachPrompt: Compare pushing a door near the hinge versus at the handle. Which case has the larger turning effect?

claim: All points on a rigid body move with the same linear speed during rotation because the body is rigid.
reality: Rigid bodies share angular velocity, not tangential speed. Linear speed depends on radius through v = r omega.
whyItHappens: Learners confuse shared angular motion with shared linear motion.
coachPrompt: On a spinning wheel, does the rim or the hub cover more distance in one second?

claim: Torque is just another word for force.
reality: Force causes translation, while torque measures the turning tendency of a force about an axis.
whyItHappens: Both are associated with pushes and pulls, so the distinction gets blurred.
coachPrompt: What changes if the same force is applied with a longer wrench?
